targeted challenger: only preprocess rewritten (parent v2). Rewrote the prompt from a rule-and-example list into an explicit five-step decomposition procedure (name quantities → resolve references against history → classify operands as cached/lookup/literal → pick the operation from the question's verb → order operands and self-check), adding coverage for verdict questions via `greater`, level-vs-change ratios, combined "X and Y" line items, enumerated-component totals, conventional constants, scale-conversion direction, impossible/typo periods, already-percent referents, and operand ordering; the three output fields, letter mapping, numeric-only program, and the existing ratio/percentage conventions are retained unchanged.
versions.rationale: The current prompt is organized as a list of output-format rules plus a gallery of percentage patterns; it teaches the agent how to *format* a program but never how to *decide* one, so every failure class here is a decision the prompt simply does not cover — which referent "that value" points at, whether an operand is a lookup or a document convention constant, whether a relation question wants a difference or a bare quotient, which operand becomes the minuend, and whether the turn is a comparison at all. Because the prompt also declares that only add/subtract/multiply/divide exist, the agent explicitly reasoned itself into emitting a subtraction on a verdict question; the calculator already exposes a `greater` tool, so admitting `greater` into the program vocabulary costs nothing downstream and removes an impossible constraint. I therefore restructured the prompt around a five-step decision procedure — name the quantities, resolve references against history, classify each operand as cached/lookup/literal, choose the operation from the question's verb, then order operands and self-check — and folded the original percentage/ratio conventions in as the final wrapper step so the output contract, the four arithmetic functions, the letter-to-sub-question mapping, the numeric-only program, and all three output fields are preserved verbatim in requirement. The generic worked shapes replace the old year-specific examples so the guidance generalizes rather than pattern-matching a handful of remembered questions.

versions.notes: targeted challenger: only preprocess rewritten (parent v2). Restructured the prompt around a five-step decomposition procedure (single-cell level lookups → reference resolution with a vacuity check → operand classification as cached level/delta/lookup/literal → operation choice from the question's verb → operand ordering and read-back), while preserving the three output fields, letter mapping, the four-function numeric-only DSL, all five original Program Design Rules, and the original worked examples verbatim. Compared with the rejected v6 it omits the `greater` operator and the speculative conjoined-metric, adjustment-qualifier, corrupted-period and percent-form rules, and restores the concrete examples v6 deleted.
versions.rationale: The current prompt is a formatting contract plus a gallery of percentage patterns: it tells the agent how to *write* a program but never how to *decide* one, so the recurring faults — re-differencing an operand that is already a delta, dividing a rate-valued metric by its own base instead of taking percentage points, phrasing a sub-question as "change in X" when the program needs X's level, phrasing one sub-question as an aggregate over two periods, collapsing a genuinely computational turn to a one-operand `A`, binding "this change" to the wrong turn, and inverting numerator/denominator — are all decisions the prompt is silent on. The previous restructure (v6) moved in the right direction (+2.29pp, P(Δ>0)=0.79) but was rejected at p=0.19 with 23 questions broken against 31 fixed, so the fix is not "more procedure" but *less collateral damage*: this rewrite keeps the procedural spine that trended positive while deliberately dropping v6's speculative and contract-touching additions — the `greater` operator (an output-contract change), the "metrics joined by and" heuristic, adjustment-qualifier decomposition, corrupted-period repair, and the percent-form re-derivation rule — and it restores v6's deleted concrete examples and the original percentage/ratio conventions verbatim, since those encode baseline-calibrated dataset behaviour. Every rule I do add is backed by at least one, mostly two, independently diagnosed failures in this batch, and I deliberately left the ×100-vs-bare-quotient policy untouched because the evidence points in both directions on identical phrasings, making any change there a coin flip that would reintroduce exactly the kind of breakage that sank v6.

versions.notes: targeted challenger: only retriever rewritten (parent v2). Restructured the prompt around lookup rather than arithmetic: added a hoisted output contract, an explicit four-step retrieval procedure, a row-disambiguation section (history qualifier inheritance, stock vs flow, total vs component), a period-alignment section with mandatory rollforward/schedule reconciliation and anti-duplication checks, a single unified sign policy defaulting to unsigned magnitudes, and a precondition list that must be satisfied before answering "not found"/"N/A"; all arithmetic, precision, formatting and field-guidance rules were preserved and moved below.
versions.rationale: The failing turns are not arithmetic or formatting failures — the current prompt spends most of its length on percentage rounding and decimal places, while giving lookup itself four bullets ("match entity and year", "don't confuse similar labels"). Every diagnosed fault is a lookup fault of one of four kinds: an invented or transcribed minus sign on a quantity that is positive by construction (contra accounts, rollforward balances, outflow lines, valuation assumptions); a column/period slip (one column of a multi-period row read twice, a header-slot figure dismissed, prose amount-period lists collapsed, a cached prior-year answer re-emitted, an off-by-one shifted year set); a premature "not found"/"N/A" when the value is present in prose or under a paraphrase or abbreviation; and a wrong row among competing labels (component instead of stated total, basic instead of the diluted variant the history had fixed, flow row instead of balance row). So I restructured rather than appended: the output contract is hoisted to the top and preserved verbatim in substance (QAPair per question, verbatim question echo, plain-string answers, program=raw/number=final, `%` only when asked, order preserved, no reasoning in the string), and the body is reorganised into an explicit retrieval procedure with the four failure classes as first-class sections — row choice, period alignment with mandatory reconciliation identities, a single unified sign policy with an explicit default and a short list of genuine exceptions, and a hard precondition list before any non-numeric answer. The arithmetic and formatting rules are retained intact but demoted below the retrieval sections so they no longer dominate the prompt's attention. No prior rewrite of this agent has been gated, so nothing here re-proposes a rejected change.

versions.notes: targeted challenger: only retriever rewritten (parent v8). Re-scoped the sign policy from a blanket strip-by-default into keep-tests-first by cell type (activity/movement rows, change-or-effect questions, and same-row sibling operands keep the printed sign; balance, contra, deduction and expense-under-subtotal lines still strip), and turned §6b from a search checklist into four preconditioned tolerances (single-series scope, qualified variant, forward-looking schedule, level-plus-change reconstruction) plus an all-N/A self-check. Rebuilt §3 as a label-priority ladder (head-noun subject, letter-for-letter abbreviations, bare class noun = balance line, inherited row for metric-less questions), added an annual-summary-vs-quarterly rule and a bidirectional uniform-shift rule to §4, and a never-expand-magnitude-words rule to §6.
versions.rationale: Two failure clusters dominate this prompt's record and they pull in opposite directions, so adding rules would not have worked — the existing sections had to be re-scoped. First, sign: v8's blanket "strip the minus" default is what fixed contra-balance cases at promotion, but it is also what broke the questions v8 lost (a rollforward "effect of others", a "net change", its percentage), and this run shows both a case needing a strip (a tax charge printed under the subtotal it reduces) and a case needing preservation (two cells of one row feeding a subtraction). I therefore reordered §5 into keep-tests-first, scoped by *cell type* rather than table type: activity/movement rows of a rollforward, change/effect questions, and same-row sibling operands keep their printed sign, while balance rows, contra accounts, deduction lines and expense/provision/tax lines under a subtotal still strip exactly as before — this preserves every strip case v8 won and un-breaks the movement-row cases it lost, and it deliberately does *not* adopt the diagnosed suggestion of "normalize only on single-lookup turns", which would have re-broken those same lost questions. Second, refusals: five of this run's faults are the retriever finding the figure and then rejecting it on a self-imposed scope, qualifier, forward-looking or period-label objection, which downstream degenerates to a non-numeric answer, so §6b now ends in four explicitly preconditioned tolerances plus an all-N/A self-check, each firing only when no competing candidate exists. The remaining faults were all "right concept, wrong line", so §3 was rebuilt as a label-priority ladder (head-noun subject vs trailing modifier or restrictive relative clause, letter-for-letter abbreviation expansion, bare class noun = level not adjustment, no-metric questions bind the inherited row while "end of <year>" names the column) with an annual-summary-vs-quarter rule added to §4 and a no-rescaling rule to §6. The output contract, history rules, arithmetic, precision, formatting and field guidance are carried over unchanged.

versions.notes: targeted challenger: only preprocess rewritten (parent v8). Kept v8's output contract, conversation-type guidance, all five Program Design Rules and the examples intact (only replacing the unevaluable `cached_ratio` token in one example with an inlined numeral), and inserted four precondition-gated sections: division of labour with the retriever (no derived-quantity sub-questions, but no collapsing a derivation into a single lookup either), reference resolution defaulting to the most recent turn with an entity-switch clause and a vacuity check, operand classification (delta vs rate vs level), and a narrow operand-order rule for two periods of one metric. Added a four-item pre-return validity checklist requiring every operand to be evaluable, forbidding empty programs/sub-question lists, and requiring the program to be read back against the reasoning; deliberately omitted the scale-direction and conversation-order rules that caused regressions in the rejected v6/v7.
versions.rationale: The current prompt is a formatting contract plus a percentage-pattern gallery: it says how to write a program but never how to decide operands, references, or the split of work with the retriever — which is where nearly every recurring fault lives (anaphor bound past the latest turn, derived-quantity sub-questions the retriever is forbidden to compute, single-lookup collapses of questions needing a derivation, already-a-delta operands re-differenced, and invented operand tokens that make the whole turn unevaluable). Two prior rewrites (v6, v7) replaced the whole prompt with a general five-step procedure and were rejected: their collateral damage was concentrated in turns that went from a correct number to the degenerate non-answer "no" and in over-firing scale/ordering rules. So this rewrite deliberately does something different: it preserves v8's spine, its five Program Design Rules and its examples verbatim (including the ×100/no-×100 conventions, which I leave completely untouched since both prior rewrites lost percent-change questions there), and adds only precondition-gated sections plus an explicit output-validity checklist. That checklist — every operand must be a letter backed by a real sub-question or a bare numeral, and neither the program nor (absent all-literal operands) the sub-question list may be empty — is new relative to both rejected attempts and targets exactly the failure signature that sank them, so it should suppress regressions rather than add them. I dropped the two rules with demonstrated collateral damage: no scale-direction rule (v7's version turned a correct "times 1000" answer into an off-by-1000 one) and no conversation-order minuend rule (v6's version flipped a correct negative change to positive); operand ordering is now stated only for the narrow, unambiguous case of two periods of the same metric, or a base the question names in words.
